replacements.from: Read together, the two misses carry the program's real finding. Development in this substrate does not funnel siblings toward a shared template, it walks each one into a region of shape space increasingly its own, which is why look-alikes become scarce with age while the width of the sibling fan grows. Commitment, measured interventionally in the steerability profile, coexists with divergence measured observationally here: each organism becomes rigid about its own course precisely while the courses spread apart.
replacements.to: Sibling shapes spread farther apart as development proceeds, and fewer pairs remain within the fixed shape-matching radius. Meanwhile, the same intervention produces less downstream change. Declining sensitivity to a push therefore coexists with growing variation among siblings.

replacements.from: The word commitment suggested a narrowing, a possibility space closing around a target form, and the basin experiment was designed to watch the narrowing happen. What the four verdicts support instead is a two-part statement: after a turn that the organism's own past announces, an equal push moves the future less and less, and at the same time nothing about the population converges, since siblings spread and look-alikes vanish. The organism does not settle into a mold. It becomes a specific individual that holds its own course against the same perturbation that once redirected it.
replacements.to: The results support a specific distinction: later bodies are less sensitive to the tested intervention, but their forms do not converge. This does not imply resistance to every intervention, and the fresh fine-shape confirmation remains unresolved.

replacements.from: A creature that cannot be pushed off course, whose siblings do not converge, and whose look-alikes disappear is not narrowing toward a template. What the visible body leaves out

The visible field adds together the matter in Flow Lenia’s channels. Different channel mixtures can therefore produce the same picture. Because those channels interact differently, a matching image need not imply a matching future.

We count simulation passages from the seeded starting field and save states at scheduled checkpoints. Repeating the comparison at later passages follows the same rule and developing field through time.

replacements.from: One instrument, which we call whole-over-parts, compares how well the full state forecasts its next state with how well the strongest tested separable split forecasts it; when this difference rises, the whole is catching up with that split, although in the prospective precursor its absolute level remains negative and the best split still forecasts better at every measured phase. This is a forecasting comparison inspired by GARD and related compositional questions, not an identification with IIT Φ.
replacements.to: To ask whether spatial regions become more informative about one another as a body forms, we compare two forecasts. One uses the measured state jointly; the other divides it into parts and treats those groups independently. We choose the strongest tested split as the comparator. The difference, which we call whole-over-parts, measures how much predictive information the joint description gains or loses relative to that split.

replacements.from: Because one score could easily mistake a convenient coordinate for a cause, we also intervened directly: we branched exact futures from the same checkpoint, applied matched writes at different ages, ran feedback policies and then released them, and swapped hidden channel composition while holding the visible field exactly fixed. The account that follows depends on where these different views agree, and it keeps their disagreements visible when they do not.
replacements.to:
If the difference rises before coherent form appears, interactions among the measured regions may be changing in a way that the outline does not capture. That is what the prospective comparison found: the joint forecast closed part of its deficit, although the best split remained ahead. The score is inspired by GARD’s whole-versus-parts question; it is not a measurement of IIT Φ.

A changing forecast does not tell us what controls development. For that, we return to the saved states and intervene. By comparing each disturbed continuation with an untouched copy, we measure the consequences of the intervention directly. Hidden-channel rewrites make this especially revealing: the initial picture can remain exactly the same while the later body changes. These comparisons connect the information measurement to a physical question about how the field maintains and changes its organization.

The earlier secondary finding is preserved below, with the confirmation and age experiments following why it remains unconfirmed.

developmental-commitment-aperture.from: The original timing hypothesis was too coarse. No next experiment has been launched.
developmental-commitment-aperture.to: The follow-up separates the fine-shape claim from the age trend: later bodies were harder to redirect while sibling shapes spread farther apart. Resistance to a disturbance and convergence on a common form must therefore be measured separately. The four completed follow-ups are reported in Commitment Increases Rigidity Without Convergence.

Does a developing body resist intervention because its possible forms are narrowing? Four experiments separate those questions. The same push had less effect at later ages, but sibling shapes spread farther apart. A fresh-cohort test also failed to confirm the earlier fine-shape result.

organism-hardens-without-narrowing.from: Steerability is the interventional face of commitment: take 64 organisms, push each one with the same local swap at ten ages spanning development, four action seeds per age, and measure how far the pushed future drifts from the untouched twin 120 steps later using the same translation-normalized shape distance throughout. The frozen prediction was that divergence is lower after the organism's structural turn than before it, with the turn computed from the untouched baseline alone as the earliest strict interior local peak of the windowed whole-minus-sum information score, declared before any outcome opened.
organism-hardens-without-narrowing.to: We applied a local swapping procedure to 64 specimens at ten ages, using four action seeds at each age, and compared their shapes with untouched copies 120 steps later. The declared prediction was a smaller response after a turn selected from the untouched baseline. The actual rule selects the highest strict interior local peak of the windowed whole-minus-sum information score, taking the earliest only in a tie. It uses both neighboring ages and the full baseline grid: the selection is independent of intervention outcomes, but is retrospective, not a signal available at the moment of the turn.

goal-state-tomography.to: We injured founder-labelled matter but judged recovery through a normalized, recentered 32×32 matter-density map, which discarded absolute mass and founder identity while retaining coarse normalized internal density. As that hidden change developed into divergent trajectories, it exposed a problem in the assay: we had followed the amplification of damage without first establishing a visible displacement from which regeneration could be measured.
